title: What Is a CDN?
sources: Cloudflare Learning Center, 'What is a CDN?' (cloudflare.com/learning/cdn/what-is-a-cdn/): a content delivery network is a geographically distributed group of servers that caches content close to end users to reduce latency; it stores copies of assets such as images, video, HTML, CSS and JavaScript

Fastly, 'What is a CDN cache?' and bunny.net academy 'What is CDN caching?': edge servers (PoPs) serve cached copies; on a cache miss the edge fetches the file from the origin server, stores a copy and serves later requests from the edge

Netflix Open Connect overview (openconnect.netflix.com/Open-Connect-Overview.pdf) and Wikipedia 'Open Connect': Netflix's own CDN places Open Connect Appliances (cache servers) inside internet service providers' networks, free to qualifying ISPs, so most streaming traffic is served locally

Latency basics: data crossing an ocean (e.g. Tokyo to New York, ~10,800 km) takes tens of milliseconds each way at the speed of light in fibre, so serving from a nearby city is faster (Cloudflare 'What is latency?')

lines.text: Yesterday we kept hot pizza by the door,
but what if your customer is in Tokyo,
and the kitchen is all the way in New York?
lines.caps: AND THE *KITCHEN | IS ALL THE *WAY | IN NEW *YORK?

lines.text: Every pizza shows up cold and late.
So the chain opens small branches in big cities,
lines.caps: SO THE *CHAIN | OPENS SMALL *BRANCHES | IN BIG *CITIES

lines.text: and you get served by the closest one.
lines.caps: AND YOU GET *SERVED | BY THE *CLOSEST ONE

lines.text: That's a CDN, a content delivery network.
It keeps copies of videos and images
on servers all over the world,
so files come from near you, not from far away.
lines.caps: SO *FILES COME | FROM *NEAR YOU | NOT FROM FAR *AWAY

lines.text: If the nearby server doesn't have it yet,
it grabs it once from the main server.
Netflix even puts its servers inside internet providers.
